sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ pīḍyamānaṃ ca mādhavam yudhiṣṭhiro 'bravīd rājan sarvasainyāni bhārata
english: Hearing that terrible roar, and that Mādhava was being hard pressed, Yudhiṣṭhira, O king, addressed all his armies, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: eṣa vṛṣṇivaro vīraḥ sātyakiḥ satyakarmakṛt grasyate yudhi vīreṇa bhānumān iva rāhuṇā abhidravata gacchadhvaṃ sātyakir yatra yudhyate
english: Yonder the foremost of the Vṛṣṇis, the hero Sātyaki, doer of true deeds, is being devoured in battle by a hero as the sun is devoured by Rāhu. Charge, hasten to where Sātyaki is fighting!

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pāñcālyam idam āha janādhipa abhidrava drutaṃ droṇaṃ kiṃ nu tiṣṭhasi pārṣata na paśyasi bhayaṃ ghoraṃ droṇān naḥ samupasthitam
english: And the lord of men spoke thus to Dhṛṣṭadyumna of the Pāñcālas: "Charge swiftly upon Droṇa! Why do you stand idle, O son of Pṛṣata? Do you not see the terrible peril that has come upon us from Droṇa?"

sanskrit: asau droṇo maheṣvāso yuyudhānena saṃyuge krīḍate sūtrabaddhena pakṣiṇā bālako yathā
english: That mighty bowman Droṇa toys with Yuyudhāna in the battle as a child toys with a bird bound by a string.

sanskrit: tatraiva sarve gacchantu bhīmasenamukhā rathāḥ tvayaiva sahitā yattā yuyudhānarathaṃ prati
english: Let all the chariot-warriors, with Bhīmasena at their head, joined with you and resolute, go there toward Yuyudhāna's chariot.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato 'nugamiṣyāmi tvām ahaṃ sahasainikaḥ sātyakiṃ mokṣayasvādya yamadaṃṣṭrāntaraṃ gatam
english: I myself, with my troops, shall follow behind you. Deliver Sātyaki today, who has passed between the very fangs of Yama.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājā sarvasainyena pāṇḍavaḥ abhyadravad raṇe droṇaṃ yuyudhānasya kāraṇāt
english: Having spoken thus, the king, the son of Pāṇḍu, then charged upon Droṇa in battle with all his army for Yuyudhāna's sake.

sanskrit: tatrārāvo mahān āsīd droṇam ekaṃ yuyutsatām pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhadraṃ te sṛñjayānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then there arose a mighty uproar—blessings upon you!—from the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas on every side, all eager to do battle with Droṇa alone.

sanskrit: te sametya naravyāghrā bhāradvājaṃ mahāratham abhyavarṣañ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavājitaiḥ
english: Those tigers among men, closing in, rained down upon the great chariot-warrior, the son of Bharadvāja, sharp arrows fledged with the feathers of heron and peacock.

sanskrit: smayann eva tu tān vīrān droṇaḥ pratyagrahīt svayam atithīn āgatān yadvat salilenāsanena ca
english: But Droṇa, smiling, received those heroes himself, as one receives guests arrived, with water and a seat.

sanskrit: tarpitās te śarais tasya bhāradvājasya dhanvinaḥ ātitheyagṛhaṃ prāpya nṛpate 'tithayo yathā
english: They were gratified by the arrows of that bowman, the son of Bharadvāja, O king, as guests are gratified on reaching a hospitable house.

sanskrit: bhāradvājaṃ ca te sarve na śekuḥ prativīkṣitum madhyaṃdinam anuprāptaṃ sahasrāṃśum iva prabho
english: And none of them could so much as look upon the son of Bharadvāja, O lord, who was like the thousand-rayed sun arrived at midday.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān maheṣvāsān droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ atāpayac charavrātair gabhastibhir ivāṃśumān
english: And Droṇa, foremost of weapon-bearers, scorched all those mighty bowmen with showers of arrows, as the sun scorches with its rays.

sanskrit: vadhyamānā raṇe rājan pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayās tathā trātāraṃ nādhyagacchanta paṅkamagnā iva dvipāḥ
english: Slain in the battle, O king, the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas alike found no deliverer, like elephants sunk in the mire.

sanskrit: droṇasya ca vyadṛśyanta visarpanto mahāśarāḥ gabhastaya ivārkasya pratapantaḥ samantataḥ
english: And Droṇa's great arrows were seen darting forth, blazing on every side like the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: tasmin droṇena nihatāḥ pāñcālāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ mahārathasamākhyātā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya saṃmatāḥ
english: In that fight twenty-five Pāñcālas were slain by Droṇa, men renowned as great chariot-warriors and esteemed by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: pāṇḍūnāṃ sarvasainyeṣu pāñcālānāṃ tathaiva ca droṇaṃ sma dadṛśuḥ śūraṃ vinighnantaṃ varān varān
english: Throughout all the armies of the Pāṇḍus and of the Pāñcālas alike, they beheld the valiant Droṇa striking down their best warriors one after another.

sanskrit: kekayānāṃ śataṃ hatvā vidrāvya ca samantataḥ droṇas tasthau mahārāja vyāditāsya ivāntakaḥ
english: Having slain a hundred of the Kekayas and driven them off on every side, Droṇa stood, O great king, like Death with gaping jaws.

sanskrit: pāñcālān sṛñjayān matsyān kekayān pāṇḍavān api droṇo 'jayan mahābāhuḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: The mighty-armed Droṇa vanquished the Pāñcālas, the Sṛñjayas, the Matsyas, the Kekayas, and the Pāṇḍavas too, by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samabhavac chabdo vadhyatāṃ droṇasāyakaiḥ vanaukasām ivāraṇye dahyatāṃ dhūmaketunā
english: From them, as they were slain by Droṇa's arrows, arose a clamor like that of forest-dwellers being burned in the woods by the fire.

sanskrit: tatra devāḥ sagandharvāḥ pitaraś cābruvan nṛpa ete dravanti pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca sasainikāḥ
english: Thereupon the gods, the Gandharvas, and the ancestors said, O king: "Yonder the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas flee with their troops."

sanskrit: taṃ tathā samare droṇaṃ nighnantaṃ somakān raṇe na cāpy abhiyayuḥ ke cid apare naiva vivyadhuḥ
english: As Droṇa thus struck down the Somakas in the fray, some would not advance against him at all, and others did not even pierce him.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā raudre tasmin vīravarakṣaye aśṛṇot sahasā pārthaḥ pāñcajanyasya nisvanam
english: As that fearful slaughter of the foremost heroes was thus proceeding, Pārtha of a sudden heard the blast of the Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: pūrito vāsudevena śaṅkharāṭ svanate bhṛśam yudhyamāneṣu vīreṣu saindhavasyābhirakṣiṣu nadatsu dhārtarāṣṭreṣu vijayasya rathaṃ prati
english: Filled with breath by Vāsudeva, the king of conches sounded loud, while the heroes who guarded the Saindhava fought on, and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra roared against the chariot of the victorious one.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvasya ca nirghoṣe vipranaṣṭe samantataḥ kaśmalābhihato rājā cintayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: And as the twang of the Gāṇḍīva died away utterly on every side, the king, the son of Pāṇḍu, smitten with dismay, fell to brooding.

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ svasti pārthasya yathā nadati śaṅkharāṭ kauravāś ca yathā hṛṣṭā vinadanti muhur muhuḥ
english: "Surely it is not well with Pārtha, the way the king of conches blares, and the way the Kauravas roar exultantly again and again."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintayitvā tu vyākulenāntarātmanā ajātaśatruḥ kaunteyaḥ sātvataṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Having pondered thus, with his inmost soul in turmoil, Ajātaśatru, the son of Kuntī, spoke to the Sātvata.

sanskrit: bāṣpagadgadayā vācā muhyamāno muhur muhuḥ kṛtyasyānantarāpekṣī śaineyaṃ śinipuṃgavam
english: In a voice choked with tears, faltering again and again, looking to what must next be done, he addressed the grandson of Śini, that bull of Śini's line.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa dharmaḥ purā dṛṣṭaḥ sadbhiḥ śaineya śāśvataḥ sāṃparāye suhṛtkṛtye tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ
english: "That eternal duty which the good of old beheld, O grandson of Śini—the service a friend renders in the hour of crisis—the time for it has now come.

sanskrit: sarveṣv api ca yodheṣu cintayañ śinipuṃgava tvattaḥ suhṛttamaṃ kaṃ cin nābhijānāmi sātyake
english: Reflecting upon all the warriors, O bull of Śini's line, I can recognize none a dearer friend than you, O Sātyaki.

sanskrit: yo hi prītamanā nityaṃ yaś ca nityam anuvrataḥ sa kārye sāṃparāye tu niyojya iti me matiḥ
english: For he who is ever loving of heart, and who is ever devoted—it is my conviction that such a one is to be appointed to a task in a time of crisis.

sanskrit: yathā ca keśavo nityaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ parāyaṇam tathā tvam api vārṣṇeya kṛṣṇatulyaparākramaḥ
english: As Keśava is ever the refuge of the Pāṇḍavas, so too are you, O Vārṣṇeya, equal to Kṛṣṇa in prowess.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ bhāraṃ samādhāsye tvayi taṃ voḍhum arhasi abhiprāyaṃ ca me nityaṃ na vṛthā kartum arhasi
english: Therefore I shall lay this burden upon you; it is for you to bear it. And my wish you ought never to render vain.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ bhrātur vayasyasya guror api ca saṃyuge kuru kṛcchre sahāyārtham arjunasya nararṣabha
english: So do you, O bull among men, render aid in this peril to my brother Arjuna in the battle—your friend and your teacher as well.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi satyavrataḥ śūro mitrāṇām abhayaṃkaraḥ loke vikhyāyase vīra karmabhiḥ satyavāg iti
english: For you are vowed to truth, a hero, a giver of fearlessness to friends; you are renowned in the world, O hero, by your deeds as a man of true word.

sanskrit: yo hi śaineya mitrārthe yudhyamānas tyajet tanum pṛthivīṃ vā dvijātibhyo yo dadyāt samam eva tat
english: For he who, fighting for a friend's sake, O grandson of Śini, lays down his body, and he who gives the whole earth to the twice-born—the two are equal.

sanskrit: śrutāś ca bahavo 'smābhī rājāno ye divaṃ gatāḥ dattvemāṃ pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ brāhmaṇebhyo yathāvidhi
english: And we have heard of many kings who went to heaven, having given this whole earth to the Brāhmaṇas according to the ordinance.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvām api dharmātman prayāce 'haṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ pṛthivīdānatulyaṃ syād adhikaṃ vā phalaṃ vibho
english: So I too beseech you, O righteous one, with joined palms: the reward shall be equal to the gift of the earth, or even greater, O mighty one.

sanskrit: eka eva sadā kṛṣṇo mitrāṇām abhayaṃkaraḥ raṇe saṃtyajati prāṇān dvitīyas tvaṃ ca sātyake
english: Kṛṣṇa alone has ever been a giver of fearlessness to friends, ready to lay down his life in battle—and you, O Sātyaki, are the second such.

sanskrit: vikrāntasya ca vīrasya yuddhe prārthayato yaśaḥ śūra eva sahāyaḥ syān netaraḥ prākṛto janaḥ
english: For a valiant hero who seeks glory in battle, only a brave man can be a fit companion—not some other, common fellow.

sanskrit: īdṛśe tu parāmarde vartamānasya mādhava tvad anyo hi raṇe goptā vijayasya na vidyate
english: And in such a crushing onslaught as is now under way, O Mādhava, there is no protector of the victorious one in battle other than you.

sanskrit: ślāghann eva hi karmāṇi śataśas tava pāṇḍavaḥ mama saṃjanayan harṣaṃ punaḥ punar akīrtayat
english: For the son of Pāṇḍu, praising your deeds a hundredfold and kindling joy in me, recounted them again and again:

sanskrit: laghvastraś citrayodhī ca tathā laghuparākramaḥ prājñaḥ sarvāstravic chūro muhyate na ca saṃyuge
english: "Swift of hand with weapons, fighting in dazzling fashion, nimble in valor, wise, knowing every weapon, a hero—he is never bewildered in battle.

sanskrit: mahāskandho mahorasko mahābāhur mahādhanuḥ mahābalo mahāvīryaḥ sa mahātmā mahārathaḥ
english: Broad of shoulder, broad of chest, mighty-armed, wielder of a great bow, of great strength and great might, that great-souled one is a great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: śiṣyo mama sakhā caiva priyo 'syāhaṃ priyaś ca me yuyudhānaḥ sahāyo me pramathiṣyati kauravān
english: My pupil and my friend as well—I am dear to him and he is dear to me. Yuyudhāna, my ally, will crush the Kauravas.

sanskrit: asmadarthaṃ ca rājendra saṃnahyed yadi keśavaḥ rāmo vāpy aniruddho vā pradyumno vā mahārathaḥ
english: And, O lord of kings, were Keśava to arm himself for our sake, or Rāma, or Aniruddha, or Pradyumna the great chariot-warrior,

sanskrit: gado vā sāraṇo vāpi sāmbo vā saha vṛṣṇibhiḥ sahāyārthaṃ mahārāja saṃgrāmottamamūrdhani
english: or Gada, or Sāraṇa, or Sāmba together with the Vṛṣṇis, to lend their aid, O great king, at the forefront of the great battle—

sanskrit: tathāpy ahaṃ naravyāghraṃ śaineyaṃ satyavikramam sāhāyye viniyokṣyāmi nāsti me 'nyo hi tatsamaḥ
english: even then I would appoint to that aid the grandson of Śini, that tiger among men of true valor; for I have no other equal to him."

sanskrit: iti dvaitavane tāta mām uvāca dhanaṃjayaḥ parokṣaṃ tvadguṇāṃs tathyān kathayann āryasaṃsadi
english: Thus, dear one, in the Dvaita forest, Dhanaṃjaya spoke to me, recounting your true qualities in your absence, in the assembly of the noble.

sanskrit: tasya tvam evaṃ saṃkalpaṃ na vṛthā kartum arhasi dhanaṃjayasya vārṣṇeya mama bhīmasya cobhayoḥ
english: You ought not, O Vārṣṇeya, to render vain such a resolve of his—of Dhanaṃjaya, and of myself and Bhīma, both of us.

sanskrit: yac cāpi tīrthāni carann agacchaṃ dvārakāṃ prati tatrāham api te bhaktim arjunaṃ prati dṛṣṭavān
english: And when, journeying on pilgrimage to the holy fords, I went toward Dvārakā, there too I beheld your devotion toward Arjuna.

sanskrit: na tat sauhṛdam anyeṣu mayā śaineya lakṣitam yathā tvam asmān bhajase vartamānān upaplave
english: Such friendship as you show us, dwelling at Upaplavya, I have marked in none other, O grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: so 'bhijātyā ca bhaktyā ca sakhyasyācāryakasya ca sauhṛdasya ca vīryasya kulīnatvasya mādhava
english: Therefore, for the sake of your noble birth and your devotion, for friendship's sake and the sake of your tutelage, for affection and valor and high lineage, O Mādhava,

sanskrit: satyasya ca mahābāho anukampārtham eva ca anurūpaṃ maheṣvāsa karma tvaṃ kartum arhasi
english: and for the sake of truth, O mighty-armed one, and out of compassion as well—it is for you, O great bowman, to do a deed befitting all this.

sanskrit: soyodhano hi sahasā gato droṇena daṃśitaḥ pūrvam eva tu yātās te kauravāṇāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: For Duryodhana has swiftly gone forth, armed, with Droṇa; and the great chariot-warriors of the Kauravas had set out before him.

sanskrit: sumahān ninadaś caiva śrūyate vijayaṃ prati sa śaineya javenātra gantum arhasi mādhava
english: And a very great roar is heard against the victorious one. Therefore, O grandson of Śini, O Mādhava, it is for you to go there with all speed.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno vayaṃ caiva saṃyattāḥ sahasainikāḥ droṇam āvārayiṣyāmo yadi tvāṃ prati yāsyati
english: Bhīmasena and I myself, made ready with our troops, will hold off Droṇa, should he move against you.

sanskrit: paśya śaineya sainyāni dravamāṇāni saṃyuge mahāntaṃ ca raṇe śabdaṃ dīryamāṇāṃ ca bhāratīm
english: Behold, O grandson of Śini, the armies fleeing in the battle, and the mighty din in the fray, and the host of the Bhāratas being torn asunder—

sanskrit: mahāmārutavegena samudram iva parvasu dhārtarāṣṭrabalaṃ tāta vikṣiptaṃ savyasācinā
english: the force of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, dear one, scattered by Savyasācin as the sea is by the rush of a great wind at the turning of the moon.

sanskrit: rathair viparidhāvadbhir manuṣyaiś ca hayaiś ca ha sainyaṃ rajaḥsamuddhūtam etat saṃparivartate
english: With chariots dashing about in all directions, and with men and with horses, this army, wrapped in the dust it has raised, whirls round and round.

sanskrit: saṃvṛtaḥ sindhusauvīrair nakharaprāsayodhibhiḥ atyantāpacitaiḥ śūraiḥ phalgunaḥ paravīrahā
english: Phalguna, the slayer of enemy heroes, is hemmed in by the men of Sindhu and Sauvīra, warriors fighting with claw-like spears and javelins, valiant and ever honored.

sanskrit: naitad balam asaṃvārya śakyo hantuṃ jayadrathaḥ ete hi saindhavasyārthe sarve saṃtyaktajīvitāḥ
english: Without first turning back this host, Jayadratha cannot be slain; for all these have laid down their lives for the Saindhava's sake.

sanskrit: śaraśaktidhvajavanaṃ hayanāgasamākulam paśyaitad dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām anīkaṃ sudurāsadam
english: Behold this army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, a forest of arrows, spears, and banners, thronged with horses and elephants, exceedingly hard to assail.

sanskrit: śṛṇu dundubhinirghoṣaṃ śaṅkhaśabdāṃś ca puṣkalān siṃhanādaravāṃś caiva rathanemisvanāṃs tathā
english: Hear the thunder of the kettledrums, and the abundant blasts of conches, and the lion-roars, and likewise the rumble of chariot-wheels.

sanskrit: nāgānāṃ śṛṇu śabdaṃ ca pattīnāṃ ca sahasraśaḥ sādināṃ dravatāṃ caiva śṛṇu kampayatāṃ mahīm
english: Hear too the noise of the elephants, and of the foot-soldiers by the thousands, and hear the horsemen as they charge, making the earth tremble.

sanskrit: purastāt saindhavānīkaṃ droṇānīkasya pṛṣṭhataḥ bahutvād dhi naravyāghra devendram api pīḍayet
english: In front is the Saindhava's host, and at the rear the host of Droṇa; by its very numbers, O tiger among men, it could press hard even upon the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: aparyante bale magno jahyād api ca jīvitam tasmiṃś ca nihate yuddhe kathaṃ jīveta mādṛśaḥ sarvathāham anuprāptaḥ sukṛcchraṃ bata jīvitam
english: Sunk within that boundless host, he might lay down his very life; and were he slain in that battle, how could one like me go on living? In every way, alas, my life has come to a most grievous pass.

sanskrit: śyāmo yuvā guḍākeśo darśanīyaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ laghvastraś citrayodhī ca praviṣṭas tāta bhāratīm
english: Dark of hue, youthful, with thick locks, fair to look upon—the son of Pāṇḍu, swift of hand and dazzling in fight, has plunged, dear one, into the host of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sūryodaye mahābāhur divasaś cātivartate tanna jānāmi vārṣṇeya yadi jīvati vā na vā kurūṇāṃ cāpi tat sainyaṃ sāgarapratimaṃ mahat
english: At sunrise the mighty-armed one went forth, and now the day is wearing away; whether he lives or not, O Vārṣṇeya, I do not know. And that army of the Kurus is vast, like the very ocean.

sanskrit: eka eva ca bībhatsuḥ praviṣṭas tāta bhāratīm aviṣahyāṃ mahābāhuḥ surair api mahāmṛdhe
english: And Bībhatsu, the mighty-armed, has plunged alone, dear one, into the host of the Bhāratas, unassailable even by the gods, in that great battle.

sanskrit: na ca me vartate buddhir adya yuddhe kathaṃ cana droṇo 'pi rabhaso yuddhe mama pīḍayate balam pratyakṣaṃ te mahābāho yathāsau carati dvijaḥ
english: And today my mind cannot rest at all upon the battle; Droṇa too, fierce in the fray, presses hard upon my force—before your very eyes, O mighty-armed one, you see how that twice-born one ranges.

sanskrit: yugapac ca sametānāṃ kāryāṇāṃ tvaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ mahārthaṃ laghusaṃyuktaṃ kartum arhasi mādhava
english: And you are skilled in tasks that crowd upon you all at once; it is for you, O Mādhava, to do the great thing, joined with swiftness.

sanskrit: tasya me sarvakāryeṣu kāryam etan mataṃ sadā arjunasya paritrāṇaṃ kartavyam iti saṃyuge
english: Of all my purposes, this has ever been the purpose I hold supreme: that the rescue of Arjuna must be accomplished in the battle.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ śocāmi dāśārhaṃ goptāraṃ jagataḥ prabhum sa hi śakto raṇe tāta trīṃl lokān api saṃgatān
english: I do not grieve for the Dāśārha, the protector of the world, its lord; for he, dear one, is able in battle to conquer even the three worlds when they stand together.

sanskrit: vijetuṃ puruṣavyāghra satyam etad bravīmi te kiṃ punar dhārtarāṣṭrasya balam etat sudurbalam
english: This I tell you in truth, O tiger among men—how much the more, then, this army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, which is so very weak.

sanskrit: arjunas tv eva vārṣṇeya pīḍito bahubhir yudhi prajahyāt samare prāṇāṃs tasmād vindāmi kaśmalam
english: But Arjuna himself, O Vārṣṇeya, pressed hard by many in the fight, might yield up his life in the battle—and therefore I am seized with dismay.

sanskrit: tasya tvaṃ padavīṃ gaccha gaccheyus tvādṛśā yathā tādṛśasyedṛśe kāle mādṛśenābhicoditaḥ
english: Go you upon his track, as those like you ought to go, urged on by one like me at such a time on behalf of such a one as he.

sanskrit: raṇe vṛṣṇipravīrāṇāṃ dvāv evātirathau smṛtau pradyumnaś ca mahābāhus tvaṃ ca sātvata viśrutaḥ
english: Of the foremost heroes of the Vṛṣṇis, two only are reckoned supreme chariot-warriors in battle: the mighty-armed Pradyumna, and you, O renowned Sātvata.

sanskrit: astre nārāyaṇasamaḥ saṃkarṣaṇasamo bale vīratāyāṃ naravyāghra dhanaṃjayasamo hy asi
english: In weapons you are the equal of Nārāyaṇa, in strength the equal of Saṃkarṣaṇa, and in heroism, O tiger among men, you are indeed the equal of Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇāv atikramya sarvayuddhaviśāradam tvām adya puruṣavyāghraṃ loke santaḥ pracakṣate
english: Passing over Bhīṣma and Droṇa, the good in the world today proclaim you, O tiger among men, the most skilled in all warfare.
